selected_modules.reason: All failures are in `gfortran.dg` tests and occur as `compile_error_before_passes`, with diagnostics like `Syntax error in CHANGE TEAM statement`, `Syntax error in FORM TEAM statement`, `Syntax error in SYNC TEAM statement`, and `Expecting END PROGRAM statement`. The issue summary explicitly asks for Fortran 2018 support for construct names on `CHANGE TEAM` and `END TEAM`, which is front-end parsing/semantic support owned by the GNU Fortran module (scanner/match/parse/resolve/coarray handling).

The original PR also mentions `Error: Name 'team_construct_name' in EXIT statement ... is unknown`, which points beyond pure tokenization to construct-name scoping and statement/block structure tracking after parsing. `tree-core` contains shared tree IR, statement-list, CFG/SSA bookkeeping, and generic lowering infrastructure that front ends can rely on when representing named constructs and control-flow targets such as `EXIT` from named constructs.

Several reproducer tests expect successful lowering visible in `-fdump-tree-original`, scanning for generated calls like `_gfortran_caf_change_team`, `_gfortran_caf_sync_team`, `_gfortran_caf_end_team`, and `_gfortran_caf_form_team`. That makes the GIMPLE/lowering boundary relevant as the intermediate representation where successful Fortran front-end translation of TEAM constructs becomes observable in tree dumps.

Although this bug is Fortran-specific, the missing feature is a named structured construct (`CHANGE TEAM` / `END TEAM`) with block-oriented control semantics similar to other structured parallel constructs. Among the shared middle-end modules, `openmp-openacc` is the closest subsystem dealing with lowering and expansion of structured parallel regions and named constructs, so it is a plausible shared dependency if construct/block handling is not entirely isolated to the Fortran frontend.
